title: HomeFlood Policies Held on More Than One Home
content:
**Rule.** A customer may hold any number of HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies, one for each home at a different property address; there is no per-customer cap. Each policy is rated, billed, renewed and cancelled on its own, and nothing on one policy is pooled into or offset against another policy of the same customer.

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a limit on how many HomeFlood policies one customer may hold? | No; there is no per-customer maximum. |
| What sets the number of policies? | One policy per home, each at a different property address. |
| Is a credit or balance on one policy used on another? | No; nothing on one policy is pooled into or offset against another. |
| Is each policy rated and billed separately? | Yes; rating, billing, renewal and cancellation run policy by policy. |

*Hypothetical illustration:* a customer insuring a primary home and a lake cottage at two different addresses holds two separate HomeFlood policies. A credit balance on the cottage policy does not reduce an amount owed on the primary-home policy.
